sn1.35:1.2: For the deities to stand in the air is disrespectful if not downright threatening ([dn3:1.21.1]()).
sn1.35:4.5: “Attentive one” is _dhīra_, one of the many terms for a wise person in Pali ([mnd9:25.4]()). It is traceable to Vedic _dhī_ (“insight, intelligence”), which famously features in the Gāyatrī Mantra as the thought, insight, or intelligence that is “spurred on” by the divine morning sun. This visionary insight is the mental faculty responsible for the creation of the hymns, driven by the poets’ quest to discern and express the hidden presence of gods (Rig Veda 1.8.6), so that the hymns themselves may therefore be called “insights” (Rig Veda 1.2.7). This heritage is still felt in Pali, where _dhīra_ is exclusively used in verse ([an4.26:1.3]()).
sn1.35:6.4: The texts usually mention the Buddha smiling when he arrives at some place of special, hidden significance ([mn81:2.1](), [mn83:2.1](), [an5.180:1.3]()). However, at [thag12.2:11.1]() he smiled when Sunīta, having gone forth from a low-born family, was honored by the gods. In both cases the Buddha smiled at the point when the gods rightly honored one who had been seen as contemptible.
sn1.35:8.3: Commentary glosses _yadi verāni na sammeyyuṁ_, suggesting a reading _na ce_, weakened for the metre.
